scope: Public evidence supports a bounded diagnosis. All execution examples are local sandboxes; merchant ownership, account access, customer consent and demand are unestablished.

contexts.name: Retail exception desk — public-reference sandbox
contexts.relationship: No ownership, engagement or permission to operate merchant accounts is claimed.
contexts.objective: Prepare accurate return/exchange exception handoffs without replacing a sufficient native route.

contexts.name: Reporting-readiness service — hypothetical sandbox
contexts.relationship: A development-assistant-authored service situation. No actual service business, buyer or customer fact is asserted.
contexts.objective: Prepare one recurring-report readiness review from an anonymized sample and a stated decision.

sources.title: FitKitty refund policy
sources.capture: Bounded extracted public text inspected through web reader; complete original page bytes and content hash are not retained in this packet.
sources.excerpt: Items from the Closet Clear-Out and Sale collections, which can be exchanged but not refunded

assertions.text: Ordinary returns already have an account self-service route.
Sale-collection items and Final Sale exclusions require care; overlap is not resolved here.
Ordinary eligibility uses delivery timing. Label dispatch and transit are treated separately.
Damage handling has separate guidance beyond the ordinary window.

limitations: Publisher policy assertions, not verified fulfillment or legal advice.
No account login or portal submission was performed.
No support-volume, handling-time or financial evidence is available.

sources.title: Hypothetical reporting-readiness scope

assertions.text: The hypothetical offer reviews one recurring report: its intended decision, cadence, source fields and an anonymized example.
A review needs the decision question, report cadence, sample description and permission to use the anonymized material.
System integration, production credentials, promised completion dates and recurring operations are outside this sample offer.

limitations: These are fictional test conditions, not observations about a real company.
Customer usefulness, demand and economic value remain unmeasured.

comparison.basis: Existing inspected fit/FAQ content weakens an absence claim. No conversion or return-reason baseline is available.
comparison.alternative: Existing product page and merchant support.
comparison.timeToProof: Public content review is immediate; commercial proof needs merchant participation and traffic.
comparison.founderBurden: Product fact-checking and permitted analytics access would be needed.

comparison.basis: Multiple policy paths allow a concrete routing test. Need frequency and avoidable handling effort remain unknown.
comparison.alternative: Native account return flow plus existing support.
comparison.timeToProof: Local task correctness and persistence are testable now; customer benefit is awaiting evidence.
comparison.founderBurden: Proposed one policy review and one sample review before any pilot.

comparison.basis: Different B2B job, inputs, output and scope; no retail rule is applicable.
comparison.alternative: A competent analyst's checklist, spreadsheet and conversation.
comparison.timeToProof: Disclosed local reuse cases now; independent buyer learning later.
comparison.founderBurden: Real adoption needs an eligible consenting operator and permitted anonymized example.

proposedIntervention.statement: A source-versioned exception handoff may reduce repeated clarification and mistaken expectations while directing ordinary cases to the existing route.
counterevidence: Existing product guidance already answers several buyer questions.
Extra intake may add effort to a sufficient workflow.
The service context is hypothetical; it supplies no demand evidence.
proposedIntervention.changeMindIf: Retain the incumbent workflow if added steps do not save useful effort, material errors appear, or an operator reports no worthwhile unmet need.
